title: A ticket's cursor crosses through one command
intention: A ticket's cursor crosses through one command that calls transitions.emit at the ticket's own component and writes the moved cursor back onto the ticket in the same act, so no voyage needs an ad hoc script to cross.
why: Peer F21 (2026-10-07): there is no CLI crossing door, so every voyage crosses through an ad hoc script that calls emit. F32 (2026-10-08) cast it next, with this measured divergence as its why: 4784351e4838's rehearsal, CLEAN before decide line D11, then raised 3, 2, 1, 4 and 9 gaps over five passes after D11-D15 — every gap on crossing machinery (emit, clear, write_verdict, predict, lacks), never on the build — and went CLEAN in one pass only once D16 ruled crossings outside a ticket's build scope. Series: CLEAN -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 9 -> CLEAN. Spend: 10 passes, $3.74, $1.98 of it the diverged five. A crossing with no standing command is machinery each ticket re-describes, and the reader treats named machinery as scope (80518446bfc8, n=1). Under RULE 1 the command berths where emit lives.
traces_to: Law 1 (a crossing is a settled act; re-deriving its script per voyage spends the resolver on the settled) and RULE 1 (crossings belong to the workflow's own component, tools/base where emit lives, not to each ticket's build or rehearsal — F32).
how: cairn/tools/base/cross.py beside cast.py: python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cross <ticket-id> <TARGET> --actor <who> --why <why> [--proven-by P ...] [--missing M ...]. It resolves the ticket in the store transitions already names (_TICKETS, overridable for a proof as cast_ticket's tickets_dir is), derives the component from the ticket's owning_intention (the charter's directory; refuses one that carries no charter), calls emit with history/state at that component and ticket=<id>, and on success writes the rendered cursor into workflow_and_state through the artifact door (verb cast). A refusal from emit prints verbatim and writes nothing. The crossing into a rest (PROVED) is refused by name: it belongs to harbor_master's clearance, a device-held machine this tool may not reach (RULE 1).

decisions.text: D1: create cairn/tools/base/cross.py. Imports: json, argparse, sys, Path; from cairn.tools.base import transitions (module, so a proof's override of transitions._TICKETS is seen); from cairn.tools.artifact.artifact import write. Signatures measured at cairn 154f7566: transitions.emit(workflow_str, target, *, history_path=None, state_path=None, node_class_root=..., **journal_extra) -> str (transitions.py:2007; raises before writing on any refusal); artifact.write(path, content, *, verb, why) (artifact.py:402). Function cross(ticket_id, target, *, actor, why, proven_by=None, missing=None, tickets_dir=None, repo_root=None) -> str: tickets_dir defaults to transitions._TICKETS, repo_root to transitions._REPO_ROOT; tp = the single match of tickets_dir.glob(f'{ticket_id}-*.json') (none -> raise ValueError naming the id); t = json.loads(tp.read_text()); wf = transitions.parse_workflow(t['workflow_and_state']); tgt = transitions.canon_target(wf, target, transitions.load_class_def(wf.node_class)); if not transitions.is_summons(tgt) and not transitions.is_disposition(tgt, <that class_def>): raise ValueError(f'{tgt} is a rest: the crossing into it is cleared by cairn.devices.cairn.machines.harbor_master.clearance.clear, not by this command'); dev = repo_root / Path(t['owning_intention']).parent; if not (dev / 'intention+why.json').is_file(): raise ValueError naming owning_intention; extra = {'ticket': ticket_id, 'actor': actor, 'why': why} plus proven_by=list and missing=list when given; new = transitions.emit(t['workflow_and_state'], target, history_path=str(dev/'history.json'), state_path=str(dev/'state.json'), **extra); if new != t['workflow_and_state']: t['workflow_and_state'] = new; write(str(tp), json.dumps(t, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why=why); return new. main(argv): argparse ticket, target, --actor (required), --why (required), --proven-by (append), --missing (append); prints the new workflow and returns 0; any exception prints f'refused: {type(e).__name__}: {e}' to stderr and returns 1. if __name__ == '__main__': sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:])). Module docstring cites 3d9cedf76a7e, F21, and set_phase(ticket=) as the write-back pattern copied.

D2 (PROOF FILE CONTENT IS QUESTION open-9989b6f514bb; BUILDME waits on its answer): create cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_crossing_runs_through_one_command.py, PROVES = {'3d9cedf76a7e': {'1': 'test_a_crossing_moves_the_cursor_and_journals_at_the_component', '2': 'test_an_illegal_target_writes_nothing', '3': 'test_proved_is_refused_naming_clearance', '4': 'test_an_owning_intention_with_no_charter_is_refused'}}. Fixture world: root = Path(scratch_dir('cross-command-fixture-')) from cairn.tools.scratch.scratch (never tempfile — the corpus tooth reds a bare temp reach); commons = root/'CairnCommons' with tickets/; repo = root/'cairn' with comp/intention+why.json ('{}') only — emit creates comp/history.json and comp/state.json when they are absent (measured 2026-10-08 at cairn 154f7566: a PROVEME->BUILDME back-edge into a fixture comp holding only the charter wrote both and returned 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME:waiting] -> PROVEME -> PROVED'); for teeth 2-4 'history+state identical' means absent before and absent after; artifact.set_diagnostic_roots({'CairnCommons': commons, 'cairn': repo}) restored in finally, as test_cast_ticket.py:296. The fixture ticket is a minimal JSON with id, owning_intention 'comp/intention+why.json' and workflow_and_state 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME] -> PROVED'; tooth 1 crosses it back to BUILDME (a back-edge is ungated) by cross(..., tickets_dir=commons/'tickets', repo_root=repo) and asserts the ticket's workflow_and_state == the return, which carries [BUILDME], and history.json gained one record naming the ticket; tooth 2 target 'NOTASTAGE' raises and ticket+history bytes are identical; tooth 3 target 'PROVED' raises with 'clearance' in the message and bytes identical; tooth 4 a ticket whose owning_intention is 'nowhere/intention+why.json' raises and bytes identical. Each tooth is also driven once through main() for its exit code (0 on tooth 1, 1 on 2-4). Run via bin/cairn test; seal with --seal.

D3: cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json gains 'cairn.tools.base.cross' in public_interface, in alphabetical place after 'cairn.tools.base.core_values', written through bin/cairn artifact write <path> --verb cast --why '3d9cedf76a7e: cross joins the public interface' --from <file>, then cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh. This ticket's build ends at the commits of D1-D3 plus D2's sealed proof; the crossings after it follow the standing code-seam@v2 workflow and are not rehearsed per ticket (as 4784351e4838 D16).

Signatures measured at transitions.py on cairn cd1a2a86: is_disposition(state: str, class_def: dict) -> bool (:547); load_class_def(node_class: str, *, root=_NODE_CLASSES) -> dict (:642); canon_target(wf: Workflow, target: str, class_def: dict | None = None) -> str (:713); parse_workflow(s) -> Workflow (:582). cross() calls parse_workflow on the ticket's workflow_and_state, load_class_def(wf.node_class), canon_target(wf, target, class_def), and refuses when the canonical target is neither a summons (is_summons) nor a disposition (is_disposition) — a rest, naming PROVED and harbor_master clearance.

The four teeth are not in the question's answer; they are written and committed at cairn cd1a2a86 in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_crossing_runs_through_one_command.py (PROVES {'3d9cedf76a7e': {'1'..'4'}}). Their contract on the build: cross.main(argv, *, tickets_dir=None, repo_root=None) returns 0 printing the new cursor as its last stdout line, or 1 printing the refusal; owning_intention resolves against repo_root (default transitions._REPO_ROOT) and the component is its parent directory, history.json and state.json there; the ticket file is <tickets_dir>/<id>-*.json. A refusal for a charterless component names the directory's repo-relative path and the word charter; the PROVED refusal names PROVED and clearance; emit's IllegalTransition message (containing 'illegal') is printed verbatim.

decisions.text: open-9989b6f514bb is answered 'yes' (recorded verbatim) to the four teeth exactly as D2 states them; D2's own text — tooth names, fixture world, assertions, main() exit codes — is the proof's complete spec, and the answer adds nothing beyond its yes. The proof file first committed at cairn cd1a2a86 was written without reading D2 and diverges from it (two tooth names, a main() taking tickets_dir/repo_root, a different fixture); it is rewritten to D2 and committed before BUILDME. cross.main(argv) takes argv only, as D1 states; the teeth call cross(..., tickets_dir=, repo_root=) and drive main() only for its exit code.

The builder never hand-edits the charter. It writes a small Python script (Write tool) that loads cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json with json.load, inserts the string 'cairn.tools.base.cross' into the public_interface list immediately after 'cairn.tools.base.core_values' (currently at line 57, before 'cairn.tools.base.crossings' at line 58), and calls cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write_json(<that path>, doc, verb='cast', why='3d9cedf76a7e: cross joins the public interface') — the same door bin/cairn artifact write --from rides, with indent=2 and ensure_ascii=False matching the file's current form; then runs cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh. The diff must show exactly one added line.

The rest refusal applies only to a target in the workflow's own path (tgt in wf.path) that is neither a summons nor a disposition; an off-vocabulary target (e.g. NOTASTAGE) is not called a rest — it goes to emit, whose IllegalTransition ('... is not in the code-seam@v2 vocabulary') is the refusal, raised before any write. D1 as written would print the false statement 'NOTASTAGE is a rest'.
